title: Relative paths in binary resources resolve incorrectly
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable, and every 4.x back to 4.0.stable
- Not reproducible in: 3.5.stable

### System information

macOS 26.6.2 - Godot v4.7.2.stable

### Issue description

`ResourceSaver.FLAG_RELATIVE_PATHS` writes a binary resource the binary loader cannot read back. The loader resolves the relative path against the path itself instead of against the file being loaded, so the path's own directory is prepended to it: 

> core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp line:635:
```python
path = ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->localize_path(path.get_base_dir().path_join(external_resources[i].path));
```
`path` and `external_resources[i].path` are the same string here.

In the attached project, `sub/outer.res` stores `../inner.tres`. Loading it gives:

```
ERROR: Cannot open file 'res://../../inner.tres'.
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://../../inner.tres.
```

The same resource saved as `.tres` loads correctly.

I found other places do it correctly:
- `resource_format_binary.cpp line:411`, same file, uses `res_path.get_base_dir()`
- `resource_format_text.cpp line:511` uses `local_path.get_base_dir()`

Introduced in 475e4ea67 (#36640) which moved this block and changed `res_path` to path. 3.5 used res_path in both places.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project
2. Open `sub/outer.res` => fails, looking for ../../inner.tres
3. Open `sub/outer.tres` => loads fine
4. make.gd regenerates both (example)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp-relative-paths.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31836387/mrp-relative-paths.zip)
